task.title: Securing IoT Devices
task.shortdesc: Secure Internet of Things (IoT) devices to prevent unauthorized access to the devices and the home network.

prereq.p: Before you secure an IoT device, make sure that:

ul.li: The is turned on and connected to the Internet.
The IoT device is available and operational.
You have the setup instructions for the IoT device.
You have access to the management application or interface for the IoT device.
You have the credentials for the .

prereq.note: Install IoT devices only from a trusted manufacturer. Make sure that the manufacturer provides security and firmware updates for the device.

context.p: IoT devices include security cameras, smart speakers, sensors, appliances, lighting controls, and home automation devices. These devices connect to the network to send or receive data.
Some IoT devices have limited security functions. An unauthorized user can use an insecure device to access the device, its data, or other network resources.
context.note: Connect only the IoT devices that you use. Disconnect or remove a device when you no longer require it.
Put IoT devices on an isolated guest or IoT network. Permit access only to the services that each device requires.

step.cmd: Review the network and security requirements of the IoT device.

ul.li: The supported Wi-Fi bands
The supported Wi-Fi security modes
The required mobile application or management interface
The firmware update method
The Internet services that the device requires

info.note: Some IoT devices support only the 2.4 GHz band. Refer to the instructions supplied with the device.

step.cmd: Check the firmware version of the IoT device.

substep.cmd: Open the management application or interface for the IoT device.
Open the device information or update settings.
Check for an available firmware update.
Install the available update.

info.note: Do not turn off the IoT device during a firmware update.

step.stepresult: The IoT device uses the available firmware version.

step.cmd: Change the default credentials of the IoT device.

substep.cmd: Open the account or security settings for the device.
Change the default username if the device permits it.
Create a 15 to 16 characters long and unique password.
Save the new credentials.

info.note: Do not continue to use the default device password.
Do not use the or the password for the as the IoT device password.

step.stepresult: The default credentials are replaced with unique credentials.

step.cmd: Enable multifactor authentication for the device account if this function is available.

info.p: Multifactor authentication requires an additional verification method when a user signs in.

step.cmd: Select an isolated network for the IoT device.

choices.choice: Connect the IoT device to a dedicated IoT network if this network is available.
Connect the IoT device to if the guest network permits the required device functions.
Connect the IoT device to only if network isolation is not available.

info.note: Some IoT devices require communication with a mobile device on the same network during the initial setup. Follow the instructions supplied with the IoT device.

step.cmd: Connect the IoT device to the selected Wi-Fi network.

substep.cmd: Open the network settings for the IoT device.
Select the applicable Wi-Fi network.
Enter the password for the selected network.
Wait for the IoT device to connect.

step.stepresult: The IoT device connects to the selected Wi-Fi network.

step.cmd: Disable device functions that you do not use.

ul.li: Remote access
Location access
Voice control
File sharing
Automatic device discovery
Unused network services

info.note: Do not disable a function that is necessary for the approved operation of the device.

step.cmd: Review the privacy settings for the IoT device.

info.p: Disable the collection or sharing of data that is not necessary for the operation of the device.
Review access to the device camera, microphone, location, contacts, and stored data when applicable.

step.cmd: Enable automatic firmware updates if this option is available.

info.p: Automatic updates help the IoT device receive available security corrections.
info.note: If automatic updates are not available, check for firmware updates regularly.

step.cmd: Configure network isolation for the IoT device.

info.p: Prevent the IoT device from accessing computers, storage devices, management interfaces, and other protected resources on the primary network.
If the supports access control rules, permit only the network communication that the IoT device requires.
info.note: Test the device after you apply an access control rule. A restrictive rule can prevent an approved device function.

step.cmd: Prevent the IoT device from accessing network management interfaces.

info.p: The IoT device must not have access to the , , or .

step.stepresult: The IoT device cannot access router management functions.

step.cmd: Create a DHCP reservation for the IoT device if a fixed address is required.

info.p: Use the MAC address of the IoT device to create the reservation in the .
info.note: A DHCP reservation is not necessary for most IoT devices. Create a reservation only when an approved application or access control rule requires a consistent IP address.

step.cmd: Confirm that the IoT device appears on the .

substep.cmd: Sign in to the .
Open the list of connected devices.
Find the IoT device in the list.
Compare the displayed device name or MAC address with the information for the IoT device.

info.note: Some devices use a private or randomized MAC address. Refer to the device network settings if the displayed address does not match the device label.

step.stepresult: The identifies the IoT device as a connected device.

step.cmd: Test the approved functions of the IoT device.

substep.cmd: Open the device application or management interface.
Confirm that the application can detect the device.
Test each required device function.
Confirm that the device cannot access protected local network resources.

step.stepresult: The IoT device operates correctly and has only the required network access.

result.p: The IoT device uses unique credentials, current firmware, and the required network connection. The device cannot access protected network resources or router management functions.

postreq.p: After you secure the IoT device:

ul.li: Check the device regularly for firmware updates.
Review the permissions and privacy settings for the device.
Review the device on the .
Remove the device from the network when you no longer use it.
Reset the device and remove stored account information before you transfer or dispose of it.
Change the device credentials if an unauthorized user obtains them.

postreq.p: If the device cannot connect after you enable network isolation, review the access restrictions. Permit only the services that the device requires.
If the device still cannot connect, see .
